title: High Frequency Eddy Current Inspection of the Fwd Lower Shell Lap Joint Fastener Rows
abstract: High frequency eddy current inspection of both fastener rows of the forward lower shell longitudinal lap joint, giving the scan coverage, the calibration requirement, the acceptance criteria and the route for reporting an indication.

sections.purpose: This task finds cracks growing from the fastener holes of the forward lower shell longitudinal lap joint between stations 1080 and 1360. It is the repetitive structural inspection called up by the maintenance programme for this zone, and one threshold and one repeat interval apply to every aircraft in the range.
sections.job_setup_note: The inspection is done from outside with the aircraft on jacks. The paint must be removed from a 60 millimetre band centred on each fastener row. Calibrate the equipment on the reference block at the start of each shift and after any probe change, and record the calibration. Surface temperature must be between 5 and 40 degrees; do not inspect in direct sunlight without a shade.
sections.procedure: 1. Put the aircraft on jacks and install the ground locks. 2. Remove the paint from a 60 millimetre band centred on each fastener row between stations 1080 and 1360. WARNING: PAINT STRIPPER CAUSES SEVERE SKIN AND EYE BURNS. WEAR THE FULL PROTECTIVE EQUIPMENT AND DO NOT LET THE STRIPPER ENTER THE CARGO COMPARTMENT DRAIN PATH. 3. Clean the surface and let it dry. 4. Calibrate the eddy current equipment on the reference block and record the trace. 5. Set the scan speed to the value given in the referenced non-destructive test manual. CAUTION: A SCAN SPEED ABOVE THE STATED LIMIT WILL HIDE SHORT INDICATIONS. 6. Scan the forward row from station 1080 to station 1360, keeping the probe normal to the surface. 7. Mark and record the position of every indication relative to the nearest frame and stringer. 8. Repeat the scan on the aft row. 9. Any indication longer than 3 millimetres makes the joint unserviceable. Report it to the manufacturer before further flight. 10. Where the splice plate ORV288354-46 is fitted, scan its outboard edge as a separate pass. 11. Where the joint is clear, restore the surface protection and the paint scheme.
sections.close_out: Restore the paint scheme and confirm the film thickness. Remove the shade and the calibration block from the area. Record the inspection, the calibration reference and the result against the aircraft. Where an indication has been reported, do not release the aircraft to service until the manufacturer has answered.

type_data.effectivity_note: All aircraft in the applicable MSN range

safety_precautions: Put the aircraft on jacks and install the ground locks.
Wear full protective equipment when you use paint stripper.
Do not let stripper enter the cargo compartment drain path.
Do not inspect in direct sunlight without a shade.

tooling.description: Eddy current equipment with 2 MHz pencil probe

title: High Frequency Eddy Current Inspection of the Fwd Lower Shell Lap Joint Fastener Rows

issue.reason: An extended repeat interval is introduced for joints re-sealed to the improved interfay standard, and the sealing standard of the joint is now recorded at close-out.

abstract: Eddy current inspection of the forward lower shell lap joint fastener rows, now carrying two repeat intervals: the original one where the interfay sealant is at the delivered standard, and a longer one where MOD-150214 has been embodied on the joint.

sections.purpose: This task finds cracks growing from the fastener holes of the forward lower shell longitudinal lap joint between stations 1080 and 1360. It is used as the repetitive inspection on unmodified aircraft and as the entry condition before the bonded strap is installed. The threshold and the repeat interval are no longer the same for every aircraft: a joint still at the delivered interfay sealing standard stays on the original interval, while a joint re-sealed under MOD-150214 is inspected at twice that interval.
